correctness.rationale: Both coordinates of a Hom cell cannot have cardinality at least two, since four distinct alternating vertices would then form a four-cycle, even if chorded. The left and right simplex families meet only at the specified oriented-edge vertices. Minimum degree two ensures their centers are distinct from those vertices. The equivariant radial retraction can be seen explicitly: in a simplex with r vertices and barycentric weights x_i, let m be the second-largest weight, including ties, and λ=max_i x_i−m. Map to weights (1−λ)/r+max(x_i−m,0). This is continuous and permutation-equivariant, lies in the center-to-vertex tree, and fixes the tree pointwise, also for r=2 and ties. Straight-line homotopy gives the required local strong retraction and fixes all shared vertices, so both coordinate swap and every automorphism commute with the glued retraction. Each oriented-edge vertex subdivides exactly one edge of the double cover; its geometric quotient by swap is G after suppressing subdivisions. The cover has 2n vertices and 2m edges; path parity gives one component for nonbipartite G and two for bipartite G, proving integral homology by graph chains. In the rational trace identity H1=H0−C0+C1 in the representation ring, no-swap fixed cover vertices and forward-oriented edges have counts 2f and 2e. Swap fixes no cover vertices; each exchanged original edge fixes both lifts with reversed orientation, giving −2s. The action on the two bipartite components is the XOR of the graph bipartition swap and the cover layer swap, giving the stated H0 terms.
residual_risks: Finite checks of mod-two Betti numbers and Lefschetz traces are corroboration, not a proof of the integral homology or equivariant strong deformation statement. Heawood results cover two specified automorphisms with both swap options, not its full automorphism group.
Graphs with leaves, isolated vertices or four-cycles are not covered by the stated literal embedding.

originality.rationale: Credit a narrow increment: the specified embedded spine in the polyhedral Hom model with a simultaneous Aut(G)×C2 strong retraction, and the explicit full action including the mixed trace. The abstract homotopy type, ordinary homology, coordinate-swap-only graph model, and its swap quotient are materially covered by the older square-free literature (especially Kamibeppu), and do not constitute novelty. The later indexed Lovász/neighborhood result also covers the no-swap trace. The inspected prior claims do not give the joint action on this embedded Hom spine, nor a statement of the full mixed character; that character is a direct chain consequence once the full model is established, not a new representation-theoretic method.
residual_risks: The Kamibeppu journal full proof was not available via the attempted lawful journal routes. The 2008 KURIMS proof sketch and the secondary comparison establish real swap-only coverage; one could ask whether a particular choice of Kamibeppu's local collapse is natural and transfers under an appropriate functorial Hom comparison. That has not been identified as the claimed embedded Hom retraction in inspected prior statements. The difference in subdivision alone is not credited.

value.rationale: The useful refinement is a simultaneous equivariant model in the original Hom space: it gives a concrete integral cycle module and controls subgroup fixed spaces and the mixed swap/automorphism action, data an unadorned graph homotopy equivalence and Betti numbers do not encode. Keeping the swap sign on endpoint-exchanged edges gives an exact character for a natural symmetry action across the full stated class, not just a computation for selected examples. Neither the already-known graph type nor the routine graph-chain trace principle alone is credited as new value.
residual_risks: No classification of Hom complexes with four-cycles or other source graphs, and no claim of a new general character formula for arbitrary CW actions.
